sentences.text: Sillosuchus was a large archosaur characterized by its long and slender neck. Shuvosaurids were bipedal, lightly armored reptiles with dinosaur-like hip and skull structures, despite being closely related to modern crocodilians.

Based on related species, shuvosaurids like Sillosuchus were likely toothless, beaked herbivores. Sillosuchus had large excavations or pockets on the sides of its neck and back vertebrae, a trait used to distinguish it from Saurosuchus.
The animal possessed short, fused ischia that were flattened top-to-bottom, unlike the side-to-side flattening seen in most other reptiles.
The cervical vertebrae of Sillosuchus had deep cavities called pleuroceli, possibly related to pneumatic structures in the axial skeleton.
Sillosuchus is the only named bipedal poposauroid known from outside North America.
The specific name longicervix refers to the genus's elongated cervical vertebrae.
The holotype specimen of Sillosuchus was discovered in the Ischigualasto Formation in the province of San Juan, Argentina.
The genus was described in 1997 by paleontologists Oscar Alcober and J. Michael Parrish.
Additional remains were first described by Dr. William Sill in 1974 but were initially attributed to the genus Saurosuchus.
A specimen (PVL 2472) contains a large isolated cervical vertebra measuring 20 cm in length.
In 2011, Nesbitt re-evaluated large fragments previously assigned to Sillosuchus and found they shared distinctive features with the holotype but were much larger.
A fossil reconstruction was presented in 2008 by the National University of San Juan as a tribute to Dr. William Dudley Sill.
Comparative studies suggest Sillosuchus likely had a light body and a bipedal posture, despite the lack of complete skull remains.
A 2026 study by Ponce, Cerda, and Desojo analyzed the histology of limb bones in Sillosuchus longicervix to investigate diverse growth rates among pseudosuchians.
Sillosuchus belongs to the family Shuvosauridae within the group Poposauroidea.

Sillosuchus is classified as a member of Poposauridae, a group of archosaurs in the clade Pseudosuchia more closely related to crocodilians than to dinosaurs, a position confirmed by a 2011 analysis by Sterling Nesbitt.
Sillosuchus is classified as a reptile.
The type species of the genus Sillosuchus is Sillosuchus longicervix.
Sillosuchus lived in South America during the Late Triassic period, specifically during the Carnian stage, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
Sillosuchus lived in a warm, seasonal environment with river-crossed alluvial plains and abundant vegetation.
It is debated whether the long neck of Sillosuchus was a unique trait or simply typical for shuvosaurids.
